name: Improper Check or Handling of Exceptional Conditions
principle: The product fails to anticipate, check, report, or handle rare error conditions. Continuing after an exceptional condition can cause crashes, unexpected state, data exposure, or unsafe fallback behavior.
detection_signals: C fgets()/fread()/read()/recv()/scanf() return value ignored before using the destination buffer
C fopen()/malloc()/calloc()/realloc()/new(std::nothrow) result used without NULL check
C ftell()/fseek()/lseek() return value ignored before casting or using size/offset
C strcpy()/strlen()/memcpy() called on a buffer populated by an unchecked I/O call
Java method declaration uses throws Exception or throws Throwable
Java catch (Exception e) or catch (Throwable t) block is empty or only logs then continues
C++ catch (...) block is empty or continues normal control flow
negative_signals: Failure-prone call result is checked with if (ret == NULL), if (ret < 0), or if (ret != expected) before use
Error branch returns, throws, goto cleanup, or otherwise prevents use of invalid output
Java method declares specific exceptions such as throws IOException, SQLException
Java/C++ catch blocks handle distinct exception types with retry, rollback, fail-closed, or rethrow
C++ RAII or Java try-with-resources guarantees cleanup on exception paths
Security decision code explicitly denies on error, e.g. return false, return 403, or throw AccessDeniedException
false_defense_traps: Checking errno without checking the failing function return value
catch (Exception e) { log(e); } followed by normal success path
throws Exception hides new exception types from callers
Initializing a buffer once but later trusting an unchecked fgets()/read() to refresh it
Default success values such as authenticated=true before a failing check
verification_focus: Does every operation that can fail have its result or exception checked before dependent state, buffers, handles, or security decisions are used?

consequence_chains.trigger: unchecked fgets() returns NULL and strcpy() later assumes a valid null-terminated buffer
consequence_chains.consequence: buffer overflow, crash, or memory corruption

consequence_chains.trigger: unchecked allocation or factory failure returns NULL and caller dereferences it
cryptographic random source failure is not reported and code falls back to weak randomness
consequence_chains.consequence: low entropy keys or predictable cryptographic material

patch_principle: Check return values and exceptions from all failure-prone I/O, allocation, parsing, and security APIs before using outputs.
Use specific exception types and specific catch blocks; rethrow or fail when the caller must decide.
Make error paths explicit: cleanup resources, return failure, throw, retry safely, or terminate.
Fail closed in authentication, authorization, cryptography, and integrity checks.
Validate partial reads/writes by comparing actual byte counts with expected byte counts.

minimal_examples.vuln: char buf[10], cp_buf[10]; fgets(buf, sizeof buf, stdin); strcpy(cp_buf, buf);
minimal_examples.safe: char buf[10], cp_buf[10]; if (fgets(buf, sizeof buf, stdin) == NULL) return; snprintf(cp_buf, sizeof cp_buf, "%s", buf);
